entries.reason: Visible source prints the chemical-space estimate as 10 with a superscript 60 (~10^60 molecules); the text layer flattens the superscript and emits the single token 1060. The output restores it as 10<sup>60</sup>, so the source's 1060 is absent and 10 and 60 appear instead. Checked on previews/page-0001.png.

The Fig. 2 caption prints the compound identifier ISM061-018-2, but the line wraps after ISM061 and the extractor swallowed the real hyphen, yielding ISM061018-2 with 018 as a bare token. The hyphen was restored after checking the visible source, so the output carries -018 where the source parser saw 018. Checked on previews/page-0004.png.
Same cause as the primary number_differences entry for this page: the restored line-wrap hyphen in ISM061-018-2 turns the source's bare 018 into -018 in the output. Checked on previews/page-0004.png.
